title: Influences of anatomy-based fitting to musical feature discrimination in adult cochlear implant users: an event-related potential study
summary:
People with severe inner ear hearing loss can often hear again with an implant in the inner ear. This implant is called a cochlear implant (CI). CI users can usually understand speech well, but have problems listening to music. For example, it is difficult to perceive the timbre. The implant manufacturer MED-EL has developed a tool which should improve listening to music. Anatomical data from the inner ear is used to improve the pitch translation in the implant. This method is called ABF (anatomy-based fitting). 
This study aims to investigate whether CI users perceive music differently with the ABF setting. To do this, two different measurement methods are used to find out whether ABF really changes the way music is heard. In the first method, we use a procedure that records electrical activity in the brain (EEG). As a further method, we want to carry out psychometric measurements. This includes tasks to identify timbre differences or distinguish between different instruments. For comparison, people with normal hearing will also carry out the measurements in order to better assess the results of CI users.
conditions: timbre perception in cochlear implant users

interventions.name:
Adult cochlear implant users with implants from Med-EL, undergo electro-physiological and psychometric measurements of timbre dicrimination skills with 2 different programming maps (with and without anatomy-based fitting) of the CI in a single sitting lasting approx. 2 hours.
Event-related potentia

Age-matched control group of normal hearing adults without CI, undergo electro-physiological and psychometric measurements of timbre dicrimination skills in one sitting, lasting approx. 1 hour. People with normal hearing serve as a control group to better assess the results of CI users.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For CI users:
• Uni- or bilateral CI treatment with an implant from MED-EL
• CI treatment for 6 months or longer
• Daily use of the CI for at least 4 hours
• Availability of an MRI or CT scan with a maximum layer thickness of 0.6 mm taken at some point prior to CI surgery
• Availability of a CT or DVT scan with a maximum layer thickness of 0.6 mm taken at some point after CI surgery
Exclusion criteria:
General exclusion criteria:
• Failure to meet the inclusion criteria
• Lack of capacity to give consent or refusal to participate in the study
• Known pre-existing conditions that affect cognition, such as dementia, depression, post-stroke condition, etc.
• Use of psychoactive medications or substances
• Intensive musical training (according to Hahne et al. (2016): duration of musical training >10 years, >3 times weekly practice within the last 3 years)

Additional exclusion criteria for CI users:
• Prelingual deafness
• Lack of auditory impression when using CI
• Usage of electrical-acoustic stimulation (CI with ipsilateral hearing aid)
• Known misplacement of the CI electrode
• Known pre-existing inner ear conditions such as cochlear malformation, otosclerosis, inner ear schwannoma
• Regular use of musical training apps developed for CI users, e.g. MELUDIA
